$comment: Gzip transfer size on the production build. Routes are DISCOVERED from the
build output, not listed here: a route that must be added by hand is a
route that will eventually be forgotten, and forgotten routes get heavy.
js.shared vs js.route exists because one `js` number conflates the
framework baseline — which we do not write — with our own client code,
which we choose every time. Reported together the framework hides our
growth. Split, the budget binds hardest on the half we control.
js.shared is effectively a tripwire for Next/React upgrades and for code
creeping into every route. js.route is the real allowance for features.
deferred bounds everything no route loads on first paint: a dynamic import
moves weight, it does not remove it, and without a limit 'lazy-loaded'
becomes a place to hide an unbounded bundle.
MOVED 5 KB from js.shared to js.route when the tree went under app/[lang].
The layout holds a Client Component (Nav), and once the layout sits below a
dynamic segment Turbopack stops hoisting it into the chunk every route
shares. Measured before and after: shared 174.8 -> 169.5, route 1.7 -> 6.4,
total 176.5 -> 175.9. Nothing got heavier — the accounting moved — so the
allowance moved with it rather than being raised.
RAISED css 8000 -> 9216 and total 300000 -> 303104 for the interaction layer.
Stated rather than absorbed quietly, because that is the only thing this
file is for. Measured after, not predicted: css 7.24 -> 7.7 KB, total 288.6 -> 289.2 KB
worst route. The additions are 13 distinct effects and
cross-document shared-element transitions, all of it CSS — js.route did not
move. The binding weights are unchanged and are not these: the font is
88 KB and the framework bundle 169.5 KB, together 257 KB of the total.
Reverting is one edit here plus removing styles/interaction.css's last two
sections; nothing else depends on it.
